set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 quality review.

Problem: ControlTransition held two throws that were unreachable only because of how their single callers happened to be written, which is a maintenance hazard rather than a live defect.
- terminal re-derived evidence by matching current.accounting and threw IllegalStateException on any case but Current, although the one caller had just set Current(record) and still held record.
- queryFailure took a whole SchedulerQueryResult and threw IllegalArgumentException on Succeeded, relying on both callers reaching it through a `case failure =>` fallthrough.

Fix, with no public shape change:
- terminal now takes the EvidenceBundle, so the caller expresses what it knows in the signature.
- queryFailure became querySplit, returning Either[(Diagnostics, EvidenceBundle), A]. Both call sites now match Right/Left instead of matching SchedulerQueryResult themselves, which is also shorter than before. A new SchedulerQueryResult case is now a compile error at one place rather than a runtime throw at two.

ControlTransition.scala now contains no throw. Evidence: all 67 managed tests pass unchanged, which is the point: the refactor is semantics-preserving and the existing suite is the check.
set.title: P8.A15: Make the two ControlTransition partial functions total
